label: Homework and grades
rationale: Schoolwork from the desk to the report card: doing homework, handing it in, working problems, good grades.
mixUps: shukudai o suru is doing it and shukudai o dasu is handing it in (or setting it, when a teacher says it); a problem you work out is toku, not kotaeru.

targets.verbSense: do; the general verb for tasks
targets.use: Said by and to students, often as a reminder or a groan: shukudai shita? or shukudai shinakya (I've got to do my homework). The o is often dropped, and yaru is just as common: shukudai yatta?
targets.notes: Getting homework is shukudai ga deru (shukudai deta), and handing it in is dasu: shukudai dashita?

example.romaji: ato de issho ni shukudai shiyou.
example.ja: 後で一緒に宿題しよう。
example.english: Let's do our homework together later.

examplePolite.romaji: ato de issho ni shukudai o shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: 後で一緒に宿題をしましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's do our homework together later.

targets.verbSense: put out, take out, send out; here: hand in, or set
targets.trap: 'Hand in' tempts watasu, which is only the physical handover to a person. Handing in work is putting it out: shukudai dashita? (teishutsu suru is the word on notices.) Who is talking tells you whether dasu means hand in or set.
targets.use: Between students it means handing in: shukudai dashita? From a teacher it means setting it, and being set homework is shukudai ga deru. Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: Forgetting it is shukudai o wasureru: shukudai wasureta.

example.english: Have you handed in the homework yet?

examplePolite.ja: 宿題はもう出しましたか？
examplePolite.english: Have you handed in the homework yet?

targets.trap: 'Solve' points to kaiketsu suru, but that's for problems in real life. Test and puzzle questions are untied: mondai o toku, and 'I got it' is toketa.
targets.use: Said about test, homework and quiz questions, often in the potential: kono mondai toketa? (did you get this one?). Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: A question that came up on a test is shiken ni deta mondai.

example.romaji: kono mondai, dou yatte toku no?
example.ja: この問題、どうやって解くの？
example.english: How do you solve this one?

examplePolite.romaji: kono mondai wa dou yatte toku n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この問題はどうやって解くんですか？
examplePolite.english: How do you solve this one?

targets.english: have good grades, do well at school
targets.trap: 'Get good grades' pushes toward a verb (ii seiseki o morau). Japanese describes the grades: seiseki ga ii. ii seiseki o toru also works for one term or exam.
targets.use: Said about kids, classmates and students, often as praise: seiseki ii ne, usually without ga. About yourself it sounds like bragging, so people say seiseki agatta (my grades went up) or play it down: seiseki yokunai.
targets.notes: ii conjugates from yoi: seiseki yokatta (past), yokunai (not good). The opposite is seiseki ga warui; falling grades are seiseki ga sagaru.

example.romaji: otouto, seiseki ii n da yo.
example.english: My little brother gets good grades.

examplePolite.romaji: otouto wa seiseki ga ii n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 弟は成績がいいんですよ。
examplePolite.english: My little brother gets good grades.

reviewPool.english: take time off work, miss work
be hooked on games; be really into games
